TopK value track effectively stayed F32, but ORT accepts F16 TopK values and scaled base-16

## Rule

**Decoded 2026-06-06 (worker-7), verified by hand on all 6 train + 1 test and by 200k truth gate.**

Count cells per color 1–9 (bg excluded). `M = max count`. **Winners** = every color tied at M
(1–3 of them in distribution). Output = `M rows × len(winners) cols`; column k = the k-th winner
**ordered by leftmost column of occurrence** in the input (all rows identical). LIVE hard caps,
mirrored in every candidate: ≤ 9 output rows (officials reach M=9: train[1] is 9×2), ≤ 3 winners.
Corpus contract (§CROP-CONTRACT, 200k): inputs **exactly 10×10**, outputs 3×1..6×3 (officials to 9×2).
§CLASS-CHECK: LIVE truth 5000/5000 ⇒ **deterministic class** — every candidate miss is a real bug.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
cnt  = [(grid == c).sum() for c in range(1, 10)]
M    = max(cnt)
wins = [c for c in range(1, 10) if cnt[c-1] == M]          # 1..3 winners
wins.sort(key=lambda c: min(np.where(grid == c)[1]))        # leftmost column order
out  = np.tile(np.array(wins), (M, 1))                      # M rows x len(wins) cols
```

   **Tail-representation lesson (the 563→543 fall)**: feeding that 243-B Equal from a u8

   Code-representation beats one-hot whenever channel-expansion can ride the final pre-Pad op.

   2×40 ([1,10] F32); M-extraction = TopK(c10,2)+Gather = 28 (8 vals + 16 dead-but-counted idx
   + 4 m) — enumerated alternatives: Slice+ReduceMax 40, Gather(iota)+ReduceMax rank-5 40,

## Don't-do log

- **Don't pre-crop the input** (crop10x10 heritage): stats off the free input cost the same and
  remove the 4,000 B crop. The two identity Gathers in LIVE were dead weight all along.
- **Don't compute counts and dominance in ONE Einsum** (`w = 1 + 16^-j`): count-scale (≤100)
  swamps f-resolution (16^-9 ≈ 4e-11) in F32 — right-side columns become indistinguishable.
- **Don't TopK an unmasked combined key** (count-primary, f-secondary): same mantissa problem.
- **The whole combined-key class is information-theoretically dead in F32** (closed 2026-06-06
  ping-1 re-sweep): one scalar holding count-order (≤100 ⇒ ~7 bits) above 10-column exponential
  leftmost-order (4 bits/column × 10) needs ~47 mantissa bits > F32's 24. A single
  `Einsum('bchw,w->bc', 16 + 16^-j)` loses all columns j ≥ 3 to rounding; rescaling only moves
  the cliff (j ≥ 4). F64 Einsum would need a 72,000 B input Cast. The Where-mask (zeroing
  losers) is precisely what keeps the two orders in SEPARATE comparisons — keep it.
- **Don't drop `valmask` hoping empty TopK slots self-mask**: ORT TopK breaks value-ties by
  LOWER index first, so with |winners|=1 the second empty slot lands on the lowest-index
  loser COLOR (not bg) and would paint a wrong column. Only slot-after-bg is safe; valmask (3 B)
  is required. (Bit-packed BitwiseAnd output expansion also enumerated: 9 active channels > 8
  u8 bits, u16 unconfirmed on CPU, u32 quadruples the inter tensor — class dead.)
- **Don't sort raw f without the ismax mask**: a loser left of a winner steals a TopK slot and
  the mask-after-sort drops a real winner.
- **#112 bit-pack + MaxPool SELECT-BY-POSITION priced DEAD vs 494** (worker w6, beta_p29, 2026-06-24,
  10-min fast-fail, no build). The prompt route (pack `pos<<k | color`, MaxPool picks largest-position
  token, mask off color) selects exactly ONE winner per pooling window. task247 emits the ORDERED set of
  up-to-3 winners simultaneously (then tiled M×K). Getting 3 ordered winners from MaxPool needs 3
  masked/iterative MaxPools = the "general sort pipeline for a small fixed winner set" the prompt
